business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common law; Gibraltar statute closely mirrors English law; ultimate civil and criminal appeal lies to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council; retained EU-derived AML/CFT and company-law standards largely continue in force
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation and Taxation Co-operation Arrangement, as updated
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters
Gibraltar Tax Information Exchange Agreement network with the UK, US, and EU member states
Gibraltar participation in the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Limited Partnerships Act 1912 (Gibraltar), as amended, including the 2014 and 2021 amendments applicable to Exempted Limited Partnerships; Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) Pt XII on persons with significant control; Limited Partnerships (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations; Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS) operated by the Registrar of Companies; Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar); Sanctions Act 2019 (Gibraltar); GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes (current edition) and the Financial Services (AML/CFT) framework rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Gibraltar Apostille Office; consular legalization via UK FCDO if the destination state is not a Hague Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Gibraltar Notary Public followed by Hague Apostille; consular legalization alternative for non-Hague destination

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening per Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) Sch 1 and the GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes: (i) identify and verify all general partners, limited partners, and ultimate beneficial owners; (ii) screen every named person and all connected corporate entities against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury UK Sanctions List, and Gibraltar domestic sanctions listings; (iii) screen for PEP status, including persons who have ceased public office within the preceding 12 months, and apply enhanced due diligence with independent source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; (iv) require certified corporate charters and ownership diagrams for any intermediate holding entity; (v) apply a documented refusal-to-act and suspicious-activity-report protocol on any sanctions match, adverse media hit, or unresolved beneficial-ownership chain.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House — Registrar of Companies online name availability and reservation portal (companieshouse.gi)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole statutory language of registration; names must be submitted in Latin/Roman script; a non-Latin name may be used only with a certified transliteration, and the registered name must remain distinguishable; the name of an Exempted Limited Partnership must end with 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', or 'L.P.'; no suffix suggesting limited-company status or government patronage is permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection the Registrar of Companies issues a written statement of grounds. The applicant, through its licensed registered agent, may file an administrative appeal within 14 days of the rejection notice, setting out why the proposed name is distinguishable and does not contravene the prohibited-token rules; the Registrar must issue a determination within 21 days. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review or statutory appeal under Part VII of the Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) within 21 days of the Registrar's decision. A fresh name application may be submitted through the portal concurrently, without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office with mail-forwarding only is not permissible for the statutory registered office; the ELP must maintain a physical registered office in Gibraltar at which process can be served, and the registered office must be held through a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider. Day-to-day operational management of a low-risk hyper-casual games publishing business may be conducted remotely from outside Gibraltar, provided central administrative control, statutory records, and governance functions operate from the Gibraltar registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — quantified at approximately 10% within the first 12 months for a non-licensed, low-risk standard ELP holding only ad-monetization payouts; the assessed likelihood rises to approximately 25% if the ELP later obtains a GFSC licence, files for Gibraltar tax residence, or becomes subject to substance-based or CFC challenges, because the Registrar and GFSC conduct unannounced on-site inspections on a risk-tiered basis.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2011 (Gibraltar), as amended, and Limited Partnerships Regulations 2011; particularly Part II (Registration) ss.5-17 and Part III (Rights and Obligations) ss.18-30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form ELP1 - Application for Registration as an Exempted Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Exempted Limited Partnership; capital contributions are fixed contractually in the Limited Partnership Agreement. No escrow account requirement is imposed at formation, subject to AML/KYC verification of all partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Exempted Limited Partnership hereby approves the admission of the Initial Limited Partner and the subscription by such partner of the full partnership interest as set forth in the Limited Partnership Agreement; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership in Gibraltar be established at the address of the licensed corporate service provider and that the Partnership Secretary/Agent be appointed; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Partner and Partnership Agent are authorised to execute all statutory forms, pay filing fees, and complete any post-registration formalities required under the Limited Partnerships Act 2011. All actions taken pursuant to this resolution are ratified and deemed effective as of the date of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written request to the Registry naming the proposed partnership. Confirm that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity and that any restricted terms are approved. Reserve the name for a period of time.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name
Full name and registered address of the proposed General Partner
Proposed registered office address in Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an alternative name for clearance or formally appeal to the Registrar requesting administrative reconsideration within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Corporate and Trust Service Provider (Gambling? Keep neutral)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider to prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement, Statement of Particulars, and consent-to-act documents. Run AML/KYC checks on all general and limited partners and verify ultimate beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter with licensed corporate service provider
AML/KYC questionnaires for all partners
Certified copies of passports/director ID and proof of address
Banking/professional references for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KYC documentation is insufficient, provide notarised or apostilled equivalents. Rectify any Registry or service provider requisition within 5 business days to avoid re-filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar (Companies House electronic filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP1 together with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement and Statement of Particulars. Pay the official filing fee. Ensure all foreign documents are apostilled if required. The General Partner and Partnership Agent must sign the statement of compliance.
required_dossiers: Form ELP1 (Application for Registration as an Exempted Limited Partnership)
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Statement of Particulars setting out partners, contributions, registered office and agent
Consent to act from the General Partner and Partnership Secretary/Agent
Certified KYC/AML dossier and apostilled identity documents of partners
Proof of payment of official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, amend the application within the specified rectification period (usually 14 days). If the period lapses, resubmit the application with a new filing date and pay the applicable resubmission fee. Refusals may be challenged by statutory review or judicial review in the Gibraltar Supreme Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registry issues the Certificate of Registration for the Exempted Limited Partnership. Verify the exact legal name, registration number, date of registration, and place of business.
required_dossiers: Registry filing receipt
Form ELP1 approval notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, notify the Registrar immediately with a letter of correction and pay any minor amendment fee. If issuance is delayed, request expedited processing through the Registrar's office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Economic Substance and Bank Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission; Income Tax Office; AML/CFT Registrar; EMI Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ELP for Gibraltar tax purposes, obtain a tax identification number, and maintain the register of beneficial owners. Complete any applicable economic substance filings and engage a Gibraltar-based licensed representative for ongoing compliance. Open a corporate bank account at a licensed Gibraltar EMI or EU-friendly bank for AdMob/AppLovin payouts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the ELP
Final executed Limited Partnership Agreement and Statement of Particulars
Proof of registered office address in Gibraltar
Tax registration forms and beneficial ownership return
AML compliance manual and risk assessment for the partnership
KYC dossier for all partners and signatories
Partnership resolutions approving bank account opening and authorised signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For GIBA/GFSC inquiries, cure by submitting supplemental declarations through the licensed representative. Reapply to alternate EMIs if initial banking onboarding is rejected; maintain current filings and good standing to avoid regulatory escalation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 5820 software publishing does not require industrial or manufacturing licensing in Gibraltar.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no onshore industrial facility; hyper-casual game publishing is digital and remote).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Registration not required; no physical establishment or stationary installations generating emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to serverless digital activity. If a future physical office is established, comply with Gibraltar's Waste Management Regulations, Air Emission Regulations, and Water Pollution Control Ordinance; no point-source wastewater, VOC, or industrial waste thresholds apply to pure software publishing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a physical office is used: Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service, structural load approval from Building Control, and workplace registration with the Office of Health and Safety. For a fully remote ELP with no physical presence, these clearances are not applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax (Income Tax Office) and Commissioner of HM Customs, jointly administered by HM Customs and Tax Division, HM Government of Gibraltar. Official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi (tax guidance and e-filing); corporate and partnership registration is lodged with the Registrar of Companies at the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), portal: https://www.fsc.gi.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-sponsored Gibraltar ELP obtains its statutory identifier as follows: (i) the foreign principals appoint a Gibraltar-licensed registered agent, who files the Exempted Limited Partnership statement under the Limited Partnerships Act 2020 with the Gibraltar Companies Registry (GFSC), electing ELP status and, if desired, separate legal personality; (ii) the Registry issues the Certificate of Registration and Registered Number, typically within 1-3 business days; (iii) the registered agent then files the ELP tax registration with the Income Tax Office, obtaining a Tax Reference Number (TRN), which is the sole statutory tax identifier; Gibraltar has no VAT ID and no separate indirect-tax registration for digital advertisers; (iv) a Customs Business Indicator is additionally required only if physical goods are imported, which is not triggered by AdMob/AppLovin digital settlements. No minimum capital is prescribed and non-resident ownership is unrestricted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - A Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act 2010: the ELP is not a chargeable person; each partner is assessed on their distributive share of ELP profits. Territorial scope: Gibraltar-resident partners are liable on worldwide income at 12.5% for corporate partners (standard rate) or applicable personal tax bands for individuals; non-resident partners are chargeable only on Gibraltar-source income. A hyper-casual gaming ELP whose management and control are located outside Gibraltar, whose publishing contracts are executed and performed abroad, and whose ad revenues are receivable offshore, is outside the charge to Gibraltar tax at both entity and non-resident-partner level, producing structurally zero Gibraltar tax liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Gibraltar statutory 'check-the-box' or partnership opacity election exists under the Income Tax Act 2010; tax transparency is mandatory for all limited partnerships. Available elections: (i) election under section 30 of the Limited Partnerships Act 2020 to confer separate legal personality on the ELP, which is fiscally neutral and does not alter transparency; (ii) for US federal tax purposes only, a multi-member ELP may file IRS Form 8832 to be classified as a partnership (or as a disregarded entity if single-member), independent of Gibraltar classification; (iii) hybrid mismatch consequences, if the ELP is dual-filed in the UK, US, or Cayman, are governed by the Income Tax (Anti-Tax Avoidance) Regulations 2021, which transpose EU ATAD-aligned hybrid rules; no election under Gibraltar law can make the ELP opaque for Gibraltar income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales-and-Use-Tax; Gibraltar operates only Import Duty and Excise Duty under the Customs Duties Act and Customs Ordinance. Digital advertising and hyper-casual mobile-game publishing revenues are outside the scope of all Gibraltar indirect taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - Gibraltar has no VAT/GST system, so no economic turnover threshold for indirect-tax registration exists; registration for customs purposes (Customs Business Indicator) is triggered from the first GIP/GBP 1 of physical imports, while digital-only publishing services incur no indirect registration. For income tax, a TRN is required from the first GIP/GBP 1 of Gibraltar-source revenue, but pure foreign-source ad settlements received by non-resident partners, absent a Gibraltar trade, are outside that requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no statutory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal-clearance API, or digital-stamping mandate. Commercial invoices and platform settlement statements issued by AdMob and AppLovin constitute sufficient documentation. Only physical imports and exports require electronic customs lodgement through HM Customs' frontier declaration gateway; these clearance procedures are not engaged by hyper-casual digital publishing and offshore advertising revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable - no VAT zero-rating claim can arise in Gibraltar because no VAT is imposed. Exports of goods from Gibraltar are outside the scope of Gibraltar import duty, and offshore digital services are automatically outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect taxation. For income-tax foreign-source substantiation, records should evidence place of effective management outside Gibraltar, contracts executed through AdMob and AppLovin outside Gibraltar, services performed outside Gibraltar, and offshore receipt of settlement funds. Gibraltar maintains no exchange-control or statutory FX-repatriation regime; the 180-day inward-remittance window is retained as a prudent substantiation benchmark.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Gibraltar HM Customs electronic export lodgement; required only for physical exports)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / electronic proof of despatch (required only for physical exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank MT103/SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing AdMob/AppLovin settlement receipts)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HM Customs and Tax Division may audit the ELP's non-residence, foreign-source, and outside-scope positions. Fraudulent or negligent under-declaration attracts civil penalties of up to 100% of the additional tax assessed, statutory interest, and, upon conviction for fraudulent evasion under the Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended), imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines. Retrospective reassessments can extend six years from the end of the charge year and are unlimited in cases of fraud or wilful default; clawback of the offshore/outside-scope position results in partner-level assessments with interest running from the original due date. In cross-border gaming structures, sham offshore management, dual-claim abuse, or inconsistent US/Gibraltar classification may disqualify the zero-tax profile and trigger penalties against both the ELP and its registered agent; anti-money-laundering and record-keeping duties under the Proceeds of Crime Act (Gibraltar) 2015 remain applicable to the licensed introducer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary anchor for Gibraltar pound and pound sterling); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the prudential and market conduct regulator; Government of Gibraltar as issuer of Gibraltar pound banknotes and coins under the Currency Notes Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar operates a fully convertible, no-exchange-control regime. The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at parity to pound sterling (GBP) and is freely interchangeable with GBP, which is also legal tender within Gibraltar. Both current account and capital account transactions are unrestricted, including non-resident ownership of capital, cross-border dividend/revenue remittances, and return of capital. No prior central bank approval, licensing, or declaration is required for profit remittance, loan repayments, or capital injections. The GFSC maintains only standard anti-money laundering (AML) monitoring and transaction reporting obligations, not foreign exchange restrictions. For a pass-through exempted limited partnership, no additional convertibility barrier exists for repatriation of gaming revenues or partner distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation applies to Gibraltar residents or entities. Export receipts, including advertising payouts from ad networks, may be retained offshore in any permitted currency without mandatory conversion to GIP/GBP. Under Gibraltar's AML framework (Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and AML Regulations 2019), only record-keeping and source-of-funds verification obligations apply for a 5-year period. There is no Central Bank mandated timeline for conversion, no minimum conversion ratio, and no exchange control surrender regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border electronic money institution (EMI) viability is moderate and requires enhanced due diligence. UK-authorised EMIs do not have automatic passporting rights into Gibraltar because Gibraltar is not part of the EEA; however, several tier-1 UK EMIs and EEA EMIs accept Gibraltar entities on a case-by-case basis under their commercial client acceptance policies. Onboarding may involve lengthier KYC subject to the ELP's beneficial ownership disclosure and a physical or quasi-physical verification step. Fully digital offshore EMIs offering multi-currency IBANs are viable for high-volume, low-value ad-network flows, but settlement finality is weaker compared to licensed local banks. Non-EEA EMIs with no regulated status in the UK/EEA are generally not acceptable for treasury-grade clearing rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar licensed banks generally mandate at least one general partner, designated partner, or senior manager to attend an in-person onboarding interview, either at the bank's premises or via an acceptable notarized/video-verified interview protocol. Remote account opening is permitted for low-risk entities provided the applicant completes a live video call with compliance officers and submits biometric ID verification, certified corporate documents, and source-of-funds evidence. For the Exempted Limited Partnership, banks will require the full list of partners, the limited partnership agreement, and a GFSC-style proof that the partnership is exempted and in good standing. Traditional banks retain discretion to demand physical presence of the general partner when the partnership is non-resident controlled or the gaming business uses multiple payout rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-layer partnership structure with a Cayman-innovation (KY) standard form ELP and non-resident partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Gibraltar Limited Partnership Act registration; statutory declaration of the general partner; full economic ownership register (PSC equivalent for partnerships); notarized passports and address proofs of all partners; org chart demonstrating absence of legal entity opacity; tax status letter confirming pass-through eligibility and no criminal/tax exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume micro-royalty and ad-network inflows from AdMob/AppLovin with cross-border settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial agreements with Google AdMob, AppLovin, and any other ad mediation platforms; monthly payout statements showing platform-to-account traceability; transaction monitoring approach; customer attribution logic and AML risk assessment for commercial counterparties; evidence that the business is not converting or layering illicit proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth of the general partner or limited partners funding the capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth declaration for each partner; bank statements demonstrating economic provenance for at least 12 months; tax returns or equivalent wealth indicators; independent legal opinion that the funds originate from lawful activities; corroboration via corporate exit documents or sale agreements if the partnership was historically funded by operating companies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gaming sector perceived as higher risk due to anonymity features and jurisdictional mismatch (UK target market, Gibraltar domicile)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed gaming compliance program under UK Advertising Codes and Apple/Google store policies; age-gating and responsible gaming controls; audited KYC/AML of end-user monetization (where applicable); evidence that hyper-casual gaming is non-regulated, offline-play style, and not gambling; proof of lawful data flows and no betting/gambling localization.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from partners into the Gibraltar ELP must be executed via high-value SWIFT MT103 wire transfers denominated in GBP, EUR, or USD. Recommended purpose codes: 'CARE' (Capital, payments of earnings and profits of a direct investment enterprise) or 'CALC' (Capital, credit between related enterprises). For partner loans, use 'CALC' or 'CANT' (capital, cancellation or repayment of credit between related enterprises) as appropriate. Banks will require the name of the foreign remitter, the ELP full legal name, the partnership's GFSC reference, and a capital account reference to segregate contributed funds. Funds must route from a regulated bank account bearing the partner's identity; crypto or third-party funding are blocked under GFSC AML guidance. Verification includes remitting bank confirmation, an internal credit memo, and reconciliation against the partnership's capital ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for trade and gaming infrastructure (server costs, subcontractors, app developers) clear via: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border, high-value payments with full adherence to purpose codes 'PROC' (payments for trade in goods and services) or 'INTC' (payments for the international trade in services); (ii) GBP Faster Payments or CHAPS for UK clearing needs; (iii) SEPA SCT credit transfers for euro-denominated EU expenses; (iv) commercial letters of credit (UCP600) for any physical or high-value procurement, established via Gibraltar licensed banks through correspondent banking relationships. All outbound wires must be supported by underlying contracts, invoices, and beneficial owner identification to satisfy GFSC transaction monitoring. No exchange control permits are required; however, banks may impose threshold reporting for payments exceeding EUR 10,000 under the Funds Transfer Regulation regime.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (up to 12 months) for USD/EUR and GBP/EUR hedging of advertising proceeds
Foreign exchange swaps for rolling short-term liquidity mismatches
Cross-currency swaps (USD/GBP/EUR) to align asset and liability cash flows at the holding level
Ban on speculative or uncovered derivatives under standard GFSC client suitability; only hedging-linked transactions acceptable
No NDF access as GIP is pegged to GBP and does not trade in local deliverable forwards for non-local currencies; NDFs are not ordinarily permissible for GIP/GBP

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal and Return of an Exempted Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of registration of the ELP; where the Registrar prescribes a calendar-year renewal cycle, by 31 December of each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of GIP 50 per month or part thereof; ongoing default for 12 consecutive months exposes the ELP to a strike-off notice and dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Registry, Gibraltar Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 January following the end of the calendar year; in addition, updates must be filed within 14 days of any transfer of a partnership interest or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to GIP 5,000; continuing contravention constitutes a criminal offence attributable to the general partner and defaulting limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, Tax Compliance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual partnership tax return, within 12 months after the end of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to GIP 10,000 for failure to notify; sustained non-compliance may lead to revocation of exempt status and exchange of information with UK and EU tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Income Tax Return and Supporting Financial Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June after the end of the year of assessment for non-resident ELPs; by the applicable return filing date for Gibraltar-resident or Gibraltar-source income activities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of GIP 100, plus monthly interest on any assessed tax; default may result in the Commissioner making a best-of-judgment assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Office and Residential General Partner or Authorised Local Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmation is submitted with the annual renewal return; any change of registered office or agent must be filed separately within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered office in Gibraltar is a statutory strike-off ground; late notification of a change may attract a penalty of GIP 100 per month.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies where the ELP exceeds Gibraltar's Companies Act audit thresholds of annual turnover above GBP 10.2 million or total gross assets above GBP 5.1 million, unless all partners unanimously agree on a qualified audit exemption; a partner or lender may also validly require an audit under the partnership agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar-adopted IFRS for larger ELPs and FRS 102 / UK GAAP equivalents for small ELPs; accounts must give a true and fair view of the partnership's profit and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Gibraltar requires the ELP to maintain a current Register of Beneficial Owners at its registered office. Each transfer of a partnership interest must be reflected in the register within 14 days. A standalone annual confirmation is due by 31 January following each calendar year and must reconcile the identity, nationality, ownership percentage, voting rights, and distribution entitlement of every beneficial owner.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners
Register of Directors of the Corporate General Partner

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar imposes a single flat corporate income tax rate of 10% on assessable profits of a trade carried on in Gibraltar. The ELP is fiscally transparent, so the charge is levied on the partners in their profit-sharing proportions. No capital gains tax applies to disposals of shares, software, game IP or digital assets. Foreign-source income of non-resident partners falls outside the Gibraltar charge where no Gibraltar trade or permanent establishment exists. There is no statutory tax holiday, but qualifying software, IT equipment and digital infrastructure expenditure may attract 100% first-year capital allowances, and trading losses may be carried forward without statutory time limit.
